TextTranslations.Research Notes: §-0012 05/27/2001\r\n\r\:
Research Notes: §-0012 05/27/2001

New artifact: Plain banana
Appearance: Just a regular yellow banana. On the large side of average. Slightly underripe,
green stem, little to no browning. Entirely unremarkable to look at. Approximately 22cm in
length, and 165g in weight. Smells ripe.

I believe the cultivar of this type of banana would be a cavendish, but I am not a pomologist.

</page>
Notes: By all accounts, this is just a normal supermarket banana. I'm not sure what else to say.
I have not physically touched the banana, but it does not appear to do anything at all. If I stare
at it long enough, my eyes start to tingle, but I wager that is just exhaustion. Nothing I do
causes anything of note. Makes me wonder why I'm even here. It's a living, I guess.

- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher
</page>
Research Notes: §-0012 05/28/2001

Artifact: Boring Banana
Appearance: Unchanged since last week

Notes: I have still not touched the banana, but all tests ran on it (chemical swabs, X-rays, MRI,
and CT scans) have come back excruciatingly unremarkable. Everything is identical to the
control banana I got from the commissary. The only notable thing I guess is that the banana
does not seem to be ripening.
</page>
It appears to be the exact same level of green that it was when it
appeared. Maybe that is indicative of something strange, but it's too early to say. Maybe this
banana did not drop out of the void after all. Maybe it just dropped off someone's lunch tray.

- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher
[DM]
TextTranslations.Research Notes: §-0012 05/30/2001\r\n\r\:
Research Notes: §-0012 05/30/2001

Artifact: Intriguing banana
Appearance: Completely the same as on day one (noteworthy)

Notes: We performed a biopsy on the banana. The biopsy itself showed us nothing except
regular banana tissue, but that's not the interesting part. To obtain the sample, we had to slice
open the skin and take a section of flesh.
</page>Two days later, the skin is sealed shut and the weight
of the banana is back to what it was pre-incision. Finally! Studying this banana so much has
started to bear fruit! Haha
</page>
Research Notes: §-0012 06/02/2001

Artifact: Self-repairing banana
Appearance: The same as day one still!

Notes: The banana has neither ripened nor decayed in any capacity, and all portions of the
banana that are removed grow back within 48 hours. Banana flesh seems to only grow back
when in contact with the skin, so removed portions themselves do not grow at all and begin to
decay at a normal rate for a chunk of banana.
</page>We began animal testing today by feeding a
portion of the banana to a mouse. Will report back tomorrow on the state of the mouse. Finally
something exciting is happening here!
</page>
Research Notes: §-0012 06/03/2001

Artifact: Banana
Appearance: The same

Notes: I'm going to be sick. I don't want to even describe what I saw in the lab today. Just
thinking about it makes me feel so nauseated that I can barely type. We shouldn't have
subjected that poor creature to this kind of suffering. If I had any idea what would happen, I
wouldn't have moved on to animal tests.
</page>I feel like a fucking monster.

- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher[DM]
TextTranslations.Research Notes: §-0012 06/05/2001\r\n\r\:
Research Notes: §-0012 06/05/2001

Artifact: Banana
Appearance: Banana

Notes: We are continuing with animal testing today despite my protests. I had a meeting with Dr
Bradley today with the intention of demanding we forgo further live tests. He listened, and he
understood my concerns. But then he reminded me that we're here for a reason, doing this
work.
</page>This technology could have a real positive impact on people around the world if we can
figure out how it works. He told me about all the lives we could save if only we could unlock the
artifact's secrets. I suppose he's right But that doesn't mean I have to like it.

- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher
</page>
Research Notes: §-0012 06/09/2001
Artifact: Banana

Notes: Today I got to meet Allison Bradley, Dr Bradley's daughter. She is an incredibly sweet
young girl with so much life in her. She wanted to observe me, and see what I do during the
work day. She also told me about her illness. She has a rare disease that prevents her skin,
and the rest of her body, from mending itself.
</page>She told me it severely limits her quality of life,
and also her life expectancy. That's why she was so interested in the strange banana.
</page>
Maybe something like that could hold the secret to fixing her body. Hearing her talk about how difficult it
is for her every day, without losing the excitement for being alive that is ever present in her
voice, made me feel something I've never really felt before. Dr Bradley was right.

This is why I'm here. This is why I do this work.
As gruesome as this entire situation is, I'd kill a thousand more mice if my research was able to
make Allison's life better.
- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher
</page>
Personal Note.

I am sick. I am not sure how much longer I will be alive. This will be my final entry about artifact
§-0012. Last week, Angela told me I have cancer. Severe. aggressive cancer, multiple types,
throughout my body. She told me she had never seen anything like it before. It started in my
hands. My skin became discolored, my joints ached, and my muscles became too weak to hold
a pen.
</page>
It has only gotten worse since then. I feel like I am falling apart on the inside. Extremely
rapid and uncontrolled cell division was the official diagnosis. All caused by that banana. I
shouldn't have held it, touched it, even looked at the damn thing. Will I end up like that first
mouse?
</page>
A writhing screaming heap of flesh? Barely recognizable as an animal at all? I don't
want to die that way. I don't want to feel my body collapsing inside of me. I'm suffering enough
already. My bones are covered in spurs and protrusions, fusing my joints together so I can
barely move. My skin is thick and rough, as if my entire body is a callous. My blood moves
sluggishly through my veins and my wounds no longer heal. I don't even recognize my
reflection in the mirror anymore.
</page>
But worst of all, I'm not the only person here who has fallen ill
in this way. Everyone on my team who was in contact with the artifact is dying too. I do not
know how much longer my heart will hold out and I don't even know if I want it to. What I do
know, is that Dr Bradley was wrong. There is no medicine to be made here. There is no
scientific advancement that can make any of this worth the cost. Their technology is built on our
Graves.

- Iris Castillo, Periphery Delta Researcher
[DM]

TextTranslations.We have uncovered a veritable infiltrati:
We have uncovered a veritable infiltration of strange roach-like creatures from beyond the lambda periphery! It appears every time we pass from one side to the other, a small number of them slip through with us.
</page>
They have started building nests in the walls and the vents. Fascinating little creatures! And very resourceful. They will pilfer and stash just about anything and everything their little bodies can carry, from paperclips to food scraps to stray bits of wire.
</page>We have cordoned off a section of our own habitat to corral and observe the roaches, in the hope of learning more about their alien physiologies. They seem to be relatively solitary despite sharing a general nesting space. They spend much of their time individually foraging for new material before returning to the communal storage area, where they eat, rest, and socialize.
</page>Though too nervous to enjoy contact with me, they are incredibly docile, and show no signs of aggression even when picked up. They just squirm in my hands until I let them go, then they promptly return to work harvesting bits and bobs from around the containment area. Sometimes I completely lose track of time just watching them scurry around. [DM]
TextTranslations.A number of the roaches have started gro:
A number of the roaches have started growing larger and exhibiting novel behaviors. A few have begun to hiss and show signs of aggression, which I assume is meant to deter predators and protect the rest of the community.
They seem particularly intent on protecting the other large roaches, which are far more interesting to me; these roaches… have started to procreate!
</page>
It appears that their reproductive system is phagic, with one large roach consuming a small one, and producing offspring from the combination of the two gene pools. I can’t wait to see what the babies end up like!

The roaches seem to have material preferences for what they like to eat. All of them will bring whatever they find, but tend to only take items they prefer. For example, one of the roaches I’ve been more closely monitoring only seems to eat bits of fabric. Another only eats crumbs from bread products. They feed each other from the stock without ration or greed. When an excess of one material builds up in the stockpile, freshly hatched roaches will take that material on as their preference, meaning everything that gets collected gets consumed without waste. A fascinating form of altruism! [DM]
TextTranslations.Astounding news from my roach observatio:
Astounding news from my roach observations! One of the little bugs has developed a copper-like coating on the exterior of its carapace! I suspect this is due to the amount of copper wires it has consumed. Perhaps each roach adapts to the singular material it eats, specializing in digesting one thing and incorporating it into its own body.

I gently captured this roach and have been feeding it only the purest copper I can get my hands on. I will continue observing how its body changes over the next few weeks. 
</page>
My copperphagic roach is now entirely encased in an outer shell of copper! The more he eats, the shinier and stronger he gets. These adaptable little creatures are unlike anything else I’ve ever studied! I intend to petition the higher-ups for more funds and more hands to grow this little operation of mine.

I'm sure there's a lot we can learn from my little buggy friends. [DM]
TextTranslations.My team and I have expanded our, and our:
My team and I have expanded our, and our little insectoid friends', horizons by offering new materials for them to consume. Our hope is that we can train them to seek out specific materials for us, to assist in the gathering of necessary supplies. Preliminary trials are highly promising! As long as the critters always return home, we can start sending them out on retrieval expeditions.

This is all going even better than I had hoped![DM]
TextTranslations.We now have an entire battalion of roach:
We now have an entire battalion of roaches each consuming different metals. Our silverphagic roach is coming along beautifully, and our gold roach has started showing external signs of metal metamorphosis as well. Once we have a stockpile of fully transformed roaches, I want to see what happens when we breed them together.

Will their offspring exhibit the traits of the parents? Can we combine these traits to create stronger adaptations? I can't wait to find out!
</page>
Our first metamorphed offspring have hatched! They appear to show traits exhibited by both parents, with a blend of material incorporated into their exoskeletons. The opportunities for new material manufacturing using these wonderful creatures are more plentiful than ever!

I’ve also gotten permission to recruit a team of other scientists to help with watching over the little buggies. [DM]
TextTranslations.This will teach me better than to trust:
This will teach me better than to trust my research to others… Someone started feeding a small group of roaches gunpowder without my permission. I only learned about it when one of them spontaneously exploded right in the center of our research lab. No humans were hurt, but several of my poor roaches perished. And now the higher ups are insisting we further develop this atrocity to create more weapons. These creatures are NOT weapons! We shouldn't be treating them like this. 
</page>
I have been removed from my own team. I did not want to turn my beloved roaches into weapons, and I'm being punished for not bending to the boss’s whims on the matter. There's nothing more I can do. I will take a selection of my favorite bugs, and I will spirit them away somewhere safe, far from these militaristic fools. I can't leave them here.[DM]
TextTranslations.Research Notes: €-0034 03/27/1999\r\n<u>:
Research Notes: €-0034 03/27/1999
<u>"Lambda Roach"</u>
Description: A small triangular insect, commonly with a brown exoskeleton. The species is Eusocial in small 'packs'.

€-0034-A (Nymphs)
Most Lambda Roaches are asexual, only taking on sexual characteristics when the pack reaches a certain size.
</page>
€-0034-B (Breeder)
During mating, one nymph takes on the dominant form and consumes its mate, metamorphosing into a post-nymph form, the breeder roach. Breeder roaches use the gametes from their devoured mate to continuously produce offspring.

The most common species of lambda roach form small flocks which occasionally escort their breeders into other flocks. This is a natural instinct to promote genetic diversity and reduce inbreeding.
</page>
€-0034-C (Soldier)
When a Breeder develops in a pack, often a few Nymphs develop into one of a few larger sterile 'Soldier' varieties. The most common soldier form is about four times the size of a normal lambda roach, and capable of jumping long distances.

</page>
<u>Adaptive Biology</u>
The Lambda Roach is a fascinating case of € xenobiology. The species is capable of harvesting material from the surrounding environment into their biology through a process not yet understood.

Through testing we have determined that they have a preference for metals, presumably to improve the strength of their exoskeleton, though with enough prodding we've been able to train them to engorge on a wide assortment of materials.

</page>
Even more interestingly, €-0034-B seems to pass on a kind of genetic preference to their offspring for materials absorbed by the parent. This simple fact may prove a powerful direction for research and open entire new approaches for material harvesting across all industries.

</page>
Commercial Uses: Varied. Strip mining, recycling, agriculture.

Military Uses: Varied. Some Nymphs have been trained to seek out explosive components to be combined within their shells. Could prove a powerful bio-weapon if explosive breeders are deployed within a city.[DM]

TextTranslations.Those idiots, who do they think they are:

The director's ration cut is NOT enough, we ought to make a public display of them all.[DM]
TextTranslations.<b>Dear residents of Habitation Green,</: Dear residents of Habitation Green, My name is Dr. Bianca Castillo and as of today, I will be taking over as director of Substructure 12 to oversee the research being performed on Periphery Kappa. I know many of you miss Dr. Rogers, as do I, but this change in leadership allows us an opportunity to explore new possibilities with fewer restrictions. Previously this facility had to operate around miles of red tape and excessive overhead that was not conducive to our mission. Starting today, I am cutting that red tape and doing away with the undue corporate scrutiny. We have an opportunity to make a real difference in the world with our research, and I do not want our ingenuity to be unnecessarily stifled. Starting today, our primary goal will be to focus our energy and resources on completing the Eden device. All other projects will be shelved for the time being, unless given proper priority clearance. With our combined expertise and some good old-fashioned hard work, together we can bring back the beautiful green earth we all remember. Once work on the Eden device is complete, we will return to the surface as heroes. Until then, let's all do our best to keep this lab working at top capacity. Thank you all for your time and attention, Dr. Bianca Castillo Director of Research Habitation Green [DM]

TextTranslations.AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynth:
AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording1_intro</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 01</color>
Okay, you got this. You got this! Hi, um. This is lead [RECORD KEEPER] Cynthia Landon, recording an official log of our expeditions into the Lambda periphery.

Photos taken within the periphery often end up corrupted and unusable, so these recordings are intended to describe the internal environment in detail.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 01</color>
Our survey probe couldn't secure any video footage, but the onboard instruments reported a generally habitable environment on the other side. And it came back in one piece.

So hopefully we will too. Next time you hear from me, I'll be on the other side.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording2_inLambda</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 02</color>
Status update: The team has successfully emerged into the Lambda periphery. Initial observations... Honestly, it's hard to find the words.

The environment is obviously alien, but it's also strangely familiar.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 02</color>
Obviously I can't feel the air through my suit, but the environment monitor say it's about 98 degrees, and my goggles are foggy.

Uh, We appear to be in a large cavern. I-I can't see the ceiling through all the plants.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 02</color>
There is no sunlight, but the plants exhibit powerful bioluminescence. It's not exactly bright in here, but it's enough to see.

I'll have to bring back samples for our bio lab to analyze. And next time, we'll bring extra flashlights.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording3_folliageReport</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 03</color>
This place is bizarre. I have to assume all the foliage is the same as normal plants, but I've never seen normal plants that glow like this.

And they come in so many different colors too, like Pink, and orange, and purple.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 03</color>
My bio-sample case is already almost full. I wonder what they use for energy. It can't be photosynthesis without a sun. Right? I'm not a biologist.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording4_animalReport</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 04</color>
Big update!

There are animals in here! It-it can be hard to spot the little ones when they hide in the foliage, but some of the others are absolutely massive.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 04</color>
They look kind of like giant bugs on stilts, and if you aren't careful, you can just walk right under them.

Now, They don't seem immediately hostile to us, but I do plan on keeping my distance.

Just in case.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording5_roaches</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 05</color>
Ugh, there are... cockroaches here. A lot of them.

Or, well, I guess they aren't actually cockroaches like we have on earth, but they're pretty similar.

Whenever I turn over a rock, or move a plant, at least one or two will just scurry out from under.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 05</color>
I'm not afraid of bugs and I have a pretty strong stomach, but I don't like these things.

They're gross and hard to catch.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording6_grubReport</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 06</color>
Found another creature. A little one this time. I nearly stepped on it. It's pink and wiggly, and almost... larval.

And That sounds gross, but it's kind of cute. Much cuter than the roaches, and also much slower.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 06</color>
If we can trap it, I'll take it in for testing. Getting a live specimen back to the labs would be a huge step forward in our understanding of this place.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording7_allergies</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 07</color>
*sniff* ugh. Not Great, I think I'm allergic to something in here. My head is pounding and my sinuses feel like they're going to implode.

Might have to dose some antihistamines or something before we come back. And, uh, maybe bring some better shoes? 
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 07</color>
The terrain is getting more treacherous the further in we go, and I'm worried I'm going to break my ankle climbing around in here.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording8_CutlerHurt</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 08</color>
Right, well done Cynthia, well done. Stupid! I think I might have jinxed us or something. Not even 5 minutes after I voiced my worry about breaking my own ankle, Cutler slipped.

I think she'll be okay, but she tore her suit and our medic says her arm is broken.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 08</color>
Anyway, Alphonso wants us to keep going deeper, but we need to get Cutler back to the medical bay for treatment.

So we're turning back for the day.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording9_bugsinSuit</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 09</color>
There are bugs in her suit! There are bugs, repeat, in her suit! Fuck! They're swarming us! I think they're drawn to the blood!

[CHIRPING]

We need to get back-[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording10_returnReport</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 10</color>
Okay, reset. This is Cynthia again. After deliberation between Alphonso and the higherups, it's been decided that our expeditions will continue.

Cutler is still recovering. Those bugs that attacked her gave her a few bites, and, um, she's got some scrapes and bruises, but the doctor says she should recover in a few days.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 10</color>
So, I'm gonna to make sure we all move a bit more carefully next time.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording11_backtoLambda</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 11</color>
Okay, fresh start. We are back in the Lambda periphery. It's mostly the same stuff as yesterday, but I think there are more creatures around.

I almost feel like we're being... watched.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 11</color>
Stupid, there's no reason to think this place has intelligent life.

Ah, I'm just - I’m Just being paranoid.
[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording12_suitIssues</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 12</color>
The pressure in my head is back.

The antihistamines don't seem to be helping much, and no one else on the team is having this problem, so maybe there's something going on with the pressure system in my suit.

I'll ask maintenance to check tonight once we get back.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 12</color>
But we can't go back until we've secured another one of those grub creatures.

The bio lab says they need another source for-[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording13_bugStalking</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 13</color>
Those bugs from yesterday are back, but they don't seem super interested in us this time. Maybe it's because no one on the team is bleeding.

It looks like they swarm in packs, and sometimes the swarm is so dense, you can’t even see through it.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 13</color>
If we get them into the specimen case together we might be... what the fuck? Al - What the fuck are you doing? Put your helmet back on![DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording14_bloodbugAttack</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 14</color>
[STATIC]
[CHIRPING]
Fuck! They're swarming him! Someone do something!
[STATIC]
What do we - I don’t know what to do! They're in his suit!
[STATIC]
What are they doing to him?
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 14</color>
[STATIC]
There’s, There's blood everywhere! Fucking go back-
[STATIC][DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording15_afterAttackReport</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 15</color>
Alphonso is dead. They couldn't stop the, um, bleeding.
[CLEARS THROAT]
So that pro-promotes me to team leader.

Not that anyone else is really willing to do take over anyway...
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 15</color>
If we give up now... He'll have died for nothing. There's something out there that will make all of this worth it.

I'm sure of it. I'm going to find it, bring it back, and make his sacrifice worth it.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording16_noMoreAccidents</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 16</color>
Okay. Today, the goal is to go deeper, and to retrieve more specimens.

We have a small team this time; just me, Mariah, Kate, and Dana. We're going to be careful and precise.

No more accidents.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording17_foundGrub</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 17</color>
We're making good progress! We found another grub, but this time, it wasn't alone.
It looks like it's being watched over by a larger bug-like creature. Maybe it's mother. 

She's too big for our specimen case, but if we observe her, she might lead us to her home.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 17</color>
If these creatures are social with each other, they might even have some kind of hive we can observe.[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording18_goingDeeper</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 18</color>
We've been following the grub creatures for a while now, deeper than we've gotten on previous excursions. They don't seem to mind us following, and I've spotted a couple others like these two.
They vary greatly in size, and the biggest I caught sight of looked like it might be bigger than a full grown human. Maybe the size of a grizzly bear?
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 18</color>
If we want to bring that one back, we'll need a much, much bigger specimen case
[DM]

AudioClip:Audio/Recordings/Cynthia/cynthia_recording19_meetMother</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 19</color>
Oh my God, OH MY GOD, Okay, okay, I was right! Th-the creatures have a central hive!
And... and oh my God, the bear-sized bug I saw earlier was not even the biggest they get.

There's one big one in the center of the hive who is absolutely massive. The rest of them seem... reverent of her.
</page>
<color=red>Transcript: Lambda Expedition Log / 19</color>
She's like a queen. Or a mother. If I can secure the necessary equipment, oh, she's definitely coming back to the lab with me.

You know... When I look at her, the pressure in my head eases a little. It almost feels like... she's trying to talk to me.
[DM]

It weighs roughly 450g and is 23.3 cm long. The creature responds to both visual and auditory stimulus, and exhibits reactions to extreme temperatures, pressure, and needle insertion. Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Picture_Grub_01 When subjected to stimulus that may cause pain, the Grub flails its body and emits an unpleasant squeaking sound. We have attempted to feed it a variety of food items, but it only seems interested in liquid nutrient slurries. Mark believes this implies it is an infant form of a larger species, but this is currently unverified. Further observation is needed. The second grub specimen in our care shows identical behavior to the initial specimen, so we have opted to dissect the superfluous creature. After draining circulatory fluid, we begin with a primary incision into the abdomen. Flesh within the grub is pale pink and white, with a texture similar to that of a cephalopod. A second bodily fluid, dull pink in color and incredibly viscous, was drained from what we assume is the cranial cavity, and has been taken to the lab for further inspection. While extracting the cranial fluid, the grub, who we had assumed to be deceased, thrashed back and forth on the table for a few moments. It did not move again after this. During this final spasm of life, the creature emitted an incredibly loud squealing noise that Dr. Macgory describes as "a piglet drowning in glue". She adds, "Don't write that down, Mark." The grub stopped moving entirely, and no longer responded to external stimuli. While we initially believed this to be a sign of impending death, Dr. Macgory is delighted to find the grub has uncurled its body and is now exhibiting the markings, coloration, and shape of a similar specimen discovered within the lambda periphery which appears to be either the 'Adult' form or simply one stage of a larger cycle. Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Classified_LambdaLabs Introductory Log - €-0331-A After months of planning, building, and negotiating, the Lambda excursion team has finally secured the cooperation of the broodmother of the 'Grub' species, €-0331, in exchange for the safe return of the living grubs currently in our possession. Though deemed a diplomatic meeting and peaceful exchange, the lab has prepared a detainment facility meant to contain the broodmother if anything goes wrong. €-0331-A will be accompanied by its human liaison Cynthia Landon, who has managed to solidify some sort of psychic rapport with the creature. We are currently unclear on how this mental communication functions, but we expect the broodmother may attempt initiation of further psychic connections with other members of the laboratory staff. In the event of undesirable outcomes from psychic interference, the biological research staff has developed an extremely potent sedative that should render €-0331-A unable to make contact. It has the added benefit of restricting movement as well. If I see any signs of insubordination, I will not hesitate to use it. Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Picture_Mother_01 Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 1 Negotiations with €-0331-A have failed after the death of Lambda liaison Cynthia Landon at the hands, or rather at the psychic whims, of the broodmother. It is suspected this attack occurred in retaliation for the five €-0331 specimens who died in our custody. Autopsy showed signs of extreme intracranial pressure, ruptures in major blood vessels, and fractures to the skull, ultimately leading to what was described by witnesses as the explosion of her head. The creature was subdued as quickly as possible by administration of the prepared sedative, but not before multiple other people present were affected by its mental onslaught. Six of the thirteen researchers present needed immediate treatment for cerebral edema and hemorrhage. One died on site, and one is left in critical condition, but the other four are expected to make full recoveries. In the meantime, the rest of Lambda labs have secured the mother in the detainment facility. It will be kept under constant surveillance and sedation to prevent further incidents. Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 3 We have started experimentation on €-0331-A with the goal of understanding its psychic abilities. The creature’s skin is thick and strong, and regenerates quickly after being damaged, but we have managed to breach the barrier to insert permanent syringes to supply a constant drip of sedative into the bloodstream. By monitoring the amount of sedative we administer, we can determine the dosage at which the mother’s consciousness and abilities are present and observable, but not strong enough to allow insubordination or damage. Ideally we can finetune a dosage at which we can use the mother’s abilities without endangering ourselves in the process. Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Picture_Mother_02 Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 6 Similar to our experimentation with the grubs, the broodmother shows reactivity to a wide variety of stimuli. It seems most reactive to electric shocks, which will be useful for controlling it during future experimentation, especially since the shocks temporarily inhibit its psychic abilities. When harvesting samples for biopsy, the creature lashed out with its mind when its hide was breached, causing multiple surrounding researchers to become dizzy and bleed from their noses. Administering an electrical shock to its body caused these symptoms to cease. Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 11 €-0331-A has been building up an immunity to the sedative. We are unable to produce it fast enough to keep raising the dosage, so we are exploring other avenues for controlling it. Our most promising option is a psychic dampening field that can cut off its ability to harm us telepathically. The technology is still under development, but I have high hopes we will be able to complete it soon. Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Picture_Mother_03 After studying what was left of Cynthia Landon’s brain, Dr. Ryhan Macgyver and his team have developed a prototype helmet that blocks one person from telepathic intrusion. It appears to work as intended, though Ryhan is too scared to allow us to test the helmet without also administering sedatives. With a bit more work, we should be able to expand that technology to protect everyone in the vicinity of €-0331-A. As long as Ryhan’s nerves don’t get in the way. Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 216 Subject €-0331-A has once again psychically bonded with one of the researchers. Using them as a conduit, the creature has asked us to release it back to the Lambda periphery. It insisted it would not hurt anyone else if we return it and all other members of €-0331 back where they came from. After deliberating, it was decided that it is more beneficial for the substructure to maintain control of the subject. There are far too many risks to releasing €-0331-A, and far too many rewards in continuing to study it. This decision was reinforced after the successful deployment of Dr. Macgyver’s anti-psionics field. There is no reason to release €-0331-A if we can control it. ^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^ ^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^ ^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^ Image:OS/Disks/Images/OS_Picture_Mother_04 Broodmother Detainment Record - Day 619 One of the other researchers wanted to know what might happen if we tried to assimilate €-0331-A LDNA into U-01. Over the course of the day’s experiments, it was discovered that subject €-0331-A is able to repel small quantities of U-01. Even while sedated or undergoing electric shock, U-01 is unable to make physical contact with the broodmother. In fact, even when a sample of U-01 is injected into it, €-0331-A is able to expel all traces of the sample from its body. This is an incredible discovery that may allow us easier extraction from U-01, or even control it entirely. Between the mother’s psychic communication and immunity to U-01, we are on the verge of some incredible discoveries down here. The ramifications of this for everyone in the substructure- and everyone up above as well- could be massive. ^^^^^ ^^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^ ^^^^^ ^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^^^ ^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^^^^ ^^^ Broodmother Detainment Record - ^^^^^ After conducting a series of experiments to observe interactions between €-0331-A and U-01, our progress has stalled. We are unable to harness or duplicate the creature’s non-axial repellant abilities. So we are ramping up our experimentation. In order to push our research farther, and to possibly wring a bit more information from €-0331-A, three grubs have been fed to U-01. They partially assimilated as expected with € biology. €-0331-A was upset by this, and made further attempts to attack our personnel and escape, but the anti-psionics technology is working exactly as intended. It appears that the mother is aware of the grubs even when they are far away. When a grub is injured on the far side of the lab, the mother becomes agitated even when it can’t see or hear the grub. This ability is severely dampened as the power of the anti-psionic field is increased, but is never fully nullified. This connection between species of €-0331 could become a very lucrative technology if we can apply it separately from €-0331-A, but as it stands, using any of the mother’s abilities has proven difficult, and we do not have enough grubs to continue using them to secure cooperation. Perhaps threats to the grubs are not enough of an incentive. Moving forward, we will have to enact harsher punishments. Broodmother Detainment Record - ^^^^^ Specimen €-0331-A has become increasingly listless and unresponsive. Not even the dissection of one of our Aunt specimens pulled the creature from this stupor. The lack of communication and cooperation is stalling our efforts here, and we are having trouble coming up with novel ways to entice the specimen into complying with our experiments. Perhaps if we turn down the anti-psionic field’s potency, we can get a bit more out of it. If not, it may be time to feed €-0331-A to U-01 entirely. Perhaps its ability to escape U-01 may neutralize it completely. If not, and our specimen of €-0331-A is consumed, then we may be able to observe the theorized promotion of an Aunt (Or other form?) into the next Broodmother. Either way, new discoveries will be made. At this point, that is all we can hope for.[DM]
